question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the plane $z=2\sqrt{5}x+2y$ that is bounded by the constraints $-1\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=2\sqrt{5}x+2y,\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2.
$$

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\sqrt{5}x+2y)=2\sqrt{5}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{5}x+2y)=2,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(2\sqrt{5})}^{2}+(2)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+20+4}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{25}\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & =5\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =5\cdot (1-(-1))\cdot (2-0) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
